narrative:
The model estimated a 49% chance that you would become a bad credit risk, which was high enough for the bank to decline the loan. Although this is close to an even chance, it still places your application on the risky side of the bank’s approval cutoff.

The most influential factor was the loan’s stated purpose. You requested credit for a used car, and among approved applicants this is a relatively less common purpose, but in your case it actually worked in your favour, pushing the decision toward good credit rather than against you. The second most important factor was your checking-account status. A balance of 0–200 DM is much less common among approved applicants than having no overdrawn or unclear checking history, and it pushed your application toward bad credit. The third factor was the amount requested. You asked for about 7,966 DM, well above the approved average of roughly 3,020 DM, and this also increased the perceived risk.

To improve a future application, consider requesting a smaller loan, building a stronger checking-account balance and reducing existing credit commitments. Ask the bank whether a guarantor or additional documentation could help, and reapply once your finances show a more stable pattern.
